behaviors.description: Parse app and runtime literal refs.
behaviors.preconditions: Literal full refs for x86_64 and aarch64.
behaviors.expected: Kind, name, arch, branch and allocating format match the literals; commit is NULL.

behaviors.description: Reject malformed full refs.
behaviors.preconditions: Empty, missing-component, invalid-kind, empty-name and extra-component inputs.
behaviors.expected: Each returns NULL and a GError.

behaviors.description: Check cached formatting and independently owned strings.
behaviors.preconditions: Live parsed app and runtime refs.
behaviors.expected: Cached pointer is stable and literal-correct; freeing one allocated string preserves the ref and cache; the other string survives ref destruction.

behaviors.description: Read explicit ref commit and collection ID from a public-property fixture.
behaviors.preconditions: Public construct-only properties supply literal values; no repository metadata is read.
behaviors.expected: Getters return the supplied 64-character commit and collection ID. This checks the Ref object contract only, not collection-ID propagation from a repository or bundle.
references: common/flatpak-ref.c: public commit and collection-id properties; flatpak_ref_get_collection_id

behaviors.description: Read related-ref policy booleans from public-property fixtures.
behaviors.preconditions: Public properties set opposite download/delete values and both autoprune values; no extension metadata is parsed.
behaviors.expected: Each getter matches its own explicit boolean. This checks policy reporting only, not extension discovery, policy derivation or transaction execution.
references: common/flatpak-related-ref.c: public should-download, should-delete, should-autoprune properties and getters

behaviors.description: Read partial and full related-ref subpaths from public-property fixtures.
behaviors.preconditions: Public subpaths property is /en,/sv or NULL; no repository or installation supplies the object.
behaviors.expected: The partial result contains exactly the two paths and terminator; full result is NULL. This checks subpath reporting only, not selection or deployment of files.

behaviors.description: Roundtrip installed-ref and remote-ref public EOL properties.
behaviors.preconditions: Constructed objects receive explicit reason/rebase properties or NULL; neither object is obtained by querying metadata.
behaviors.expected: All four getters return the literal properties, including NULL. This partial getter test earns no installed or remote EOL metadata requirement credit.
references: common/flatpak-installed-ref.c: public end-of-life properties and getters
common/flatpak-remote-ref.c: public end-of-life properties and getters

behaviors.description: Roundtrip public AppStream-related object properties.
behaviors.preconditions: Constructed objects receive literal version, MIT license, OARS type and two rating attributes or NULL; no AppStream document is loaded.
behaviors.expected: Version, license, type and complete rating map match the supplied properties; missing values return NULL. This partial getter test earns no AppStream metadata requirement credit.
references: common/flatpak-installed-ref.c: public appdata properties and getters

behaviors.description: Retain owned URL and explicitly referenced borrowed metadata.
behaviors.preconditions: Remote URL setter and RemoteRef public metadata property supply literals.
behaviors.expected: URL and retained bytes remain byte-exact after both source objects and original input bytes are released.

behaviors.description: Parse valid and malformed flatpakrepo bytes.
behaviors.preconditions: Literal Version=1 file and three malformed files; isolated user installation.
behaviors.expected: Name, URL and title match literals without adding a remote; malformed files return NULL and errors.

behaviors.description: Keep uncommitted remote changes local to the object.
behaviors.preconditions: One unadded object and one configured remote.
behaviors.expected: The unadded name is absent; edited object's URL changes while a newly opened installation still returns the original URL.

behaviors.description: Refresh remote configuration cached by an installation.
behaviors.preconditions: A second installation object commits a different URL.
behaviors.expected: Dropping original object's caches succeeds and its next lookup returns the changed literal URL.

behaviors.description: Reject duplicate remote addition without replacement.
behaviors.preconditions: Existing unfiltered remote and same-name object with changed URL/title.
behaviors.expected: FALSE with FLATPAK_ERROR_ALREADY_INSTALLED; reopened URL/title remain original.

behaviors.description: Accept duplicate if-needed addition without replacement.
behaviors.preconditions: Existing unfiltered remote and same-name object with changed URL/title.
behaviors.expected: TRUE without error; reopened URL/title remain original.

behaviors.description: Persist descriptive remote properties.
behaviors.preconditions: Configured unsigned remote with literal comment, description, homepage and icon edits.
behaviors.expected: All four getters return edited literals after reopening.

behaviors.description: Persist independent remote policy booleans.
behaviors.preconditions: All eight disabled/noenumerate/nodeps combinations, then all FALSE.
behaviors.expected: Reopened getters match every combination and the final reset.
references: common/flatpak-remote.c: disabled, noenumerate and nodeps setters/getters

behaviors.description: Persist GPG verification policy.
behaviors.preconditions: Remote without a collection ID; verification TRUE then FALSE.
behaviors.expected: Both values survive reopening and collection ID remains NULL.

behaviors.description: Check local branch and collection-ID edits.
behaviors.preconditions: Remote object gets explicit string values followed by NULL.
behaviors.expected: Getters return literal strings then NULL. No signed-repository persistence credit is claimed.

behaviors.description: Persist filter pathname and main ref.
behaviors.preconditions: Valid allow-rule filter file and explicit full app ref.
behaviors.expected: Reopened getters return the supplied path and literal ref.

behaviors.description: Clear a persisted filter through if-needed addition.
behaviors.preconditions: Persisted filter is first verified; same-name replacement explicitly sets NULL filter.
behaviors.expected: if-needed addition succeeds and a reopened remote has NULL filter.

behaviors.description: Filter remote enumeration by public type.
behaviors.preconditions: One configured static remote.
behaviors.expected: STATIC yields exactly the fixture and its STATIC type; USB/LAN yields an empty array.

behaviors.description: Persist and unset both documented language configuration keys.
behaviors.preconditions: Literal semicolon-separated languages and extra-languages values.
behaviors.expected: Reopening returns each exact value; NULL unsetting yields NULL with G_KEY_FILE_ERROR_KEY_NOT_FOUND.

behaviors.description: Resolve configured languages and territory-bearing extra locales.
behaviors.preconditions: Explicit de;fr, then unset languages with de_DE;fr_CA extra-languages, then empty languages.
behaviors.expected: Explicit arrays contain exactly de/fr; extra locale territories survive while languages include de/fr; empty languages gives an empty array.

behaviors.description: Select the user installation and retain its owned path.
behaviors.preconditions: Runner-controlled HOME/XDG environment.
behaviors.expected: is_user TRUE, ID user, path equals configured user location and remains usable after installation release.

behaviors.description: Observe Unix-second remote configuration timestamps.
behaviors.preconditions: Remote addition and title edit separated by two seconds; the public installation directory is then temporarily moved away.
behaviors.expected: Available timestamps are bounded by wall-clock seconds and the edit advances the timestamp; unavailable location yields G_MAXUINT64.

behaviors.description: Keep custom user installation queries separate from default user state.
behaviors.preconditions: Fixture app/runtime installed in default user location; distinct empty custom path.
behaviors.expected: Custom constructor reports its supplied path and TRUE user profile; its ref list is empty while default list is exactly the app/runtime; custom configuration survives reopening.

behaviors.description: Load application override metadata configured through the public CLI.
behaviors.preconditions: CLI override --user sets two literal environment values for the fixture app and a different value for another app.
behaviors.expected: The public library loader returns parseable override metadata with exactly the fixture app's two Environment keys and literal values, including spaces and an equals sign. Assertions do not depend on backend paths or keyfile serialization.

behaviors.description: Check canonical default and ordered supported architectures.
behaviors.preconditions: Runner has verified fixture architecture against target machine.
behaviors.expected: Default and first supported architecture equal fixture arch; all entries are canonical and unique; x86_64 priority is x86_64 then i386; array terminates.

behaviors.description: Check public error-domain identities.
behaviors.preconditions: No installation required.
behaviors.expected: Flatpak and portal quarks are nonzero, stable and distinct.

mappings.rationale: Both literal ref kinds have all identity components, formatting and absent commit asserted.
All malformed inputs require NULL and a non-NULL error, including missing component and invalid kind.
Literal equality, borrowed pointer stability, independent frees, live-ref inspection and post-destruction owned-string inspection are asserted.

The requirement's explicit-ID ref fixture is supplied through the public collection-id property and verified by the getter. Credit covers object-level exposure only; this does not verify repository or bundle metadata propagation.

Autoprune explicitly permits public-property fixtures. Download/delete getters remain useful property checks but receive no metadata-to-policy derivation credit here; that contract is tested by queryx-related-policy using actual extension declarations.

The public subpaths property supplies the fixture's declared partial set; exact paths and terminator, plus NULL for all files, are asserted through the getter. This covers object-level reporting, not subpath selection from metadata or partial deployment.

Owned URL survives remote destruction; borrowed metadata is explicitly reffed before source destruction and byte-checked after all source references are released. The public metadata property supplies bytes solely for this lifetime contract; no metadata retrieval pipeline is claimed.
Valid file name/URL/title and installation absence are checked; three invalid files require NULL and error.
Unadded name remains absent and an uncommitted URL edit is visible only on the edited object.
Second installation commits changed URL; original installation drops caches and observes that literal change.
Checks failure domain/code and preservation of both URL and title after reopening.
Checks success and preservation of both URL and title despite different same-name input values.
Committed comment, description and homepage are each checked against literals on a newly opened installation.
All independent boolean combinations and final FALSE reset are checked after reopening.
TRUE then FALSE survive reopening on a verified collection-ID-free remote.
Valid filter pathname and explicit main ref are committed and checked after reopening.
Checks initial persisted filter and its removal by explicit NULL filter on if-needed addition.
STATIC enumeration has exactly the configured name and STATIC type; USB/LAN enumeration succeeds empty.
Both supported keys roundtrip exact semicolon strings across reopening and each NULL unset yields the documented missing-key error.
Explicit language arrays, territory-preserving extra locales, language-only extra codes and empty-string all-languages semantics are asserted.
User profile, ID and independently expected path are checked; owned GFile is used and released after installation destruction.

Available timestamps must lie in Unix-second wall-clock bounds and advance after a remote change beyond timestamp resolution; temporarily moving the entire public installation directory away must yield G_MAXUINT64.
Custom path/user identity and empty queries contrast with the exact two installed default-user refs.

CLI override --user seeds two known environment values and a decoy app's different value. The public library loader must return parseable metadata containing exactly the requested app's two Environment keys and literal values; no private paths or serialization details are assumed.
Fixture architecture supplies independent expected default; canonical names, termination and x86_64 compatibility priority are asserted.
Both domain functions are called repeatedly and asserted nonzero, stable and mutually distinct.
